own_tests.input: preprocess on grayscale (L), RGBA, palette (P), LA, and a 1x1 image
own_tests.result: All return a finite float32 tensor of shape (3,224,224).

own_tests.input: End-to-end train() with convnext_tiny (pretrained=False, patched), 12 real COCO jpgs (8 train, 4 dev), CPU forced via torch.cuda.is_available=False, 2 epochs, then resume from latest.pt with epochs=3
own_tests.result: Fresh run: epochs_done=2, ckpt epoch=2, sched last_epoch=2, AdamW step=4 (2 batches x 2 epochs). Resume ran only epoch 3 (history epochs [3]); ckpt epoch=3, sched last_epoch=3, AdamW step=6, so epoch, optimizer and scheduler state continue rather than restart.

own_tests.input: Fresh train() into a dir that already has checkpoints; resume at an already-finished epoch; resume after the manifest changed
own_tests.result: Fresh: FileExistsError. Resume at end: returns epochs_done=3 with empty history and best.pt present. Changed manifest: ValueError 'trained on a different manifest'.

own_tests.input: JPEG with EXIF orientation 6 through preprocess
own_tests.result: No exif_transpose is applied in preprocess, so rotated phone photos are not corrected. T2.1 does not list orientation (#30 is a later item), so I record it as a note only.

notes: 1) test_resume_requires_explicit_path only checks epochs/history; breaking optimizer and scheduler restore leaves all tests green (verified by mutation). Consider adding an assertion on resumed optimizer step or lr. 2) On resume the scheduler state dict restores the old T_max, so extending epochs on resume (e.g. 2->3) makes the cosine LR rise again (lr 5e-4 at epoch 3, T_max still 2). Resuming with an unchanged config is fine. 3) build_loaders reseeds random and torch at the start of every train() call, so a resumed run repeats the epoch-0 shuffle and augmentation draws instead of continuing the RNG stream. This does not break correctness but is not a bit-exact resume. 4) preprocess does no EXIF transpose; the future prediction task (#30) must handle orientation. 5) My first, accidental run of a debug script (steps.py) was not forced to CPU and used the GPU briefly for a tiny 2-epoch job; the reported CPU results come from the rerun with cuda disabled. 6) The convnext_tiny pretrained download path is only covered by a @pytest.mark.real test that was not run.
